Workflow

I sketched. Figma Make prototyped. Cursor built. I directed, selected, and styled. The decisions were mine — the execution was shared. A continuous back-and-forth, not a linear process.

Core Feature

The review loop

Each level has its own chat. The trainer reviews the submission, previews the level content, then approves — unlocking the next level — or returns it for correction. Feedback stays in context.

Approve Return Under review Locked

Design Decision

One photo per level

We worked this out with the trainer. With 20 students, each sending 3–4 photos per level — that adds up. One photo slot, replaceable. Plus two text messages for context. Simple constraint, clear result.

Design System

DS·80

80 components · 15 sections · Generated by Cursor · Styled by the designer

Learnings

What I took away

01

The status logic didn't come together at once

The hardest part was mapping how all the statuses connect. I kept adding things, fixing dependencies, and iterating until the logic finally clicked. It was gradual — not something I figured out in one go.

02

AI is a good executor, not a decision-maker

Some AI suggestions were off. Others were genuinely good. The workflow only worked because there was always a designer selecting, directing, and deciding. The taste and judgment stayed human throughout.

03

The one-photo rule came from a real conversation

Constraints that fit the domain work better than open flexibility. This one came from sitting with the trainer and thinking through what actually happens when you have 20 students submitting work at the same time.
